title: Protocol for Studying Reprogramming of Mouse Pancreatic Acinar Cells to β-like Cells
protocol: Optimize an ex vivo protocol for isolation, adenoviral infection, and culturing of primary exocrine cells for up to 8 days.
Isolate primary pancreatic exocrine cells using the optimized protocol.
Sacrifice mice by cervical dislocation.
Place a 6-well plate with 4 mL of cold HBSS wash solution per well on ice.
Dissect and excise the pancreas into a single well containing HBSS wash solution.
Wash the tissue in the well and transfer to a new well containing cold HBSS wash solution.
Transfer one pancreas into a 60 mm tissue culture plate with 5 mL of cold collagenase solution.
Mince the tissue with scissors.
Gently transfer minced tissue to a 50 mL conical tube using a trimmed pipettor.
Incubate for 12 minutes at 37°C.
Pipette the tissues gently five times up and down using a 1 mL trimmed pipette after the first 4 minutes of incubation, repeating every 2 minutes until the end of the incubation.
Add 45 mL of ice cold HBSS wash solution to each tube containing digested pancreas.
Centrifuge the cells at 200 × g for 3 minutes and then aspirate the supernatant.
Add an additional 45 mL of HBSS wash solution, mix, and centrifuge again at 200 × g for 3 minutes.
Gently resuspend the pellet in 5 mL HBSS wash solution using a 1 mL trimmed pipette.
Add HBSS wash solution to achieve a total volume of 30 mL.
Filter through a standard metal tea strainer followed by filtration through a 100 μm cell strainer.
Centrifuge at 200 × g for 3 minutes and aspirate the supernatant, leaving approximately 3 mL of liquid.
Reconstitute alloxan stock solution immediately before use.
Dilute alloxan stock solution 1:100 (10 mM) in HBSS wash solution.
Prepare three 15 mL conical tubes, each containing 9 mL of HBSS+alloxan.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 3 mL HBSS wash solution.
Transfer 1 mL of resuspended cells to each of the prepared 15 mL conical tubes containing alloxan solution.
Incubate for 10 minutes at room temperature (20°–30°C).
Allow cell clusters to sediment by gravity.
Inject 270 μl of leptan working solution to deliver 0.0675 mg of leptan (2.5 mg/kg body weight).
Aspirate alloxan solution leaving ∼1 mL at the bottom of the tube.
Resuspend the cell pellet with trimmed 1 mL pipette tip and transfer cells from each tube to a new 15 mL tube containing 9 mL of HBSS wash solution.
Allow cell clusters to sediment by gravity for 7 minutes.
Repeat the last step, combining three tubes containing cells from the same pancreas into one 15 mL tube.
Aspirate the HBSS wash solution from the 15 mL conical tube leaving a minimal volume at the bottom.
Resuspend the cells gently using a trimmed 1 mL pipette tip and resuspend in 3 mL of Waymouth’s culture medium in a 50 mL conical tube.
Mix cells gently by swirling the conical tube and immediately transfer 100 μL of cells to an Eppendorf tube.
Wash the cells twice with PBS by centrifugation of the cells at 500 × g for 4 min.
Lyse the cells using 100 μL of lysis buffer.
Measure protein concentration using Bio-Rad protein assay.
Calculate the protein concentration in the original tube containing cells.
Dilute the cells to a final concentration of 1,700 μg protein equivalent/mL with Waymouth’s medium.
Add 1.5 mL of Waymouth’s medium to the desired amount of wells in 6-well plates (non-collagen coated at this stage).
To each well add 0.5 mL of cell suspension.
Continually and gently swirl the tube containing the cells while plating to uniformly mix them.
Transfer the plates to a standard tissue culture incubator (37°C, 5% CO2) while preparing the adenoviruses for infection.
Infect exocrine cell clusters with adenoviral vectors Ad-PDX1 and Ad-NGN3 to induce reprogramming to the somatostatin δ cell lineage.
Add Ad-MafA to the mix of Ad-PDX1 and Ad-NGN3 for reprogramming to the insulin-expressing β cell lineage.
Infect exocrine cell clusters with a single viral vector expressing all three PNM factors (Ad-M3-mCherry) for predominantly insulin-expressing cells formation.
Calibrate the titer for each new viral vector before use, considering that different vectors achieve maximal expression at different titers and some compromise cell viability at high titers.
Prepare a mix containing the desired volume of virus stocks in 50 μL Waymouth’s medium per well.
Use final titers as specified for infections in a 6-well plate with cells in 2 mL medium.
Vortex the virus mix well.
Remove the plate containing the cells from the incubator and add 50 μl of the virus mix to each well.
Mix well by swirling the plate gently.
Put the plate back into the incubator.
Swirl the plate once more just before placing it inside the incubator to evenly distribute the cells.
Incubate the cells for 16–24 h.
Collect cell suspension from each well using a 1 mL trimmed pipette tip into a 15 mL tube.
Allow cells to sediment by gravity for 8 minutes to deplete dead cells.
Aspirate the maximum amount of media, leaving the cell pellet at the bottom.
Prepare a new 15 mL tube containing 9 mL of Waymouth’s medium.
Collect the cell pellet using a 1 mL trimmed pipette tip and gently add it to the top layer of media in the new tube.
Allow cells to sediment by gravity for 8 minutes to deplete dead cells.
Aspirate the maximum amount of media, leaving the cell pellet at the bottom.
Resuspend the cell pellet in Waymouth’s medium in the desired volume for plating.
For volumes larger than 3 mL, use 50 mL conical tubes and mix by swirling.
Do not mix cells by pipetting up and down to avoid damaging exocrine cell clusters integrity and viability.
Plate the cells on collagen-coated plates according to the desired subsequent application.
For RNA extraction, plate cells on 6-well or 24-well plates.
Cells from each infected well can be plated on four wells of a 24-well plate.
Plate cells on 24-well plates for immunofluorescence.
Or plate cells on 4-well μ slides (ibidi) or on wells containing collagen-coated plastic coverslips for immunofluorescence.
Do not use glass coverslips as cells do not attach well to them.
Plate cells on 12-well plates for insulin secretion assay.
Plate cells from each infected well of a 6-well plate onto two wells of 12-well plates.
For applications requiring large numbers of cells, such as flow cytometry or ChIP, plate cells on 10 cm culture dishes.
All cells from a 6-well plate should be plated on one 10 cm culture dish for these applications.
Continuously mix the tube containing the cells by gentle swirling during plating to avoid uneven distribution of cells between wells.
Transfer plates to a standard tissue culture incubator (37°C, 5% CO2).
Change the medium after 48 hours: most cell clusters will attach to the plate by this time.
Aspirate the old medium containing dead cells and unattached cell clusters.
Add fresh medium to the plates.
Change the medium every other day thereafter.
Harvest cells with Tri-reagent at the desired time point for endocrine gene expression analysis by qPCR.
Perform RNA isolation and cDNA synthesis using standard protocols.
Assess RNA integrity if analysis is required before day 3 in culture.
Perform qRT-PCR with desired primers for endocrine genes.
Aspirate the medium.
Fix cells for 12 min in 4% PFA.
Wash cells three times with PBST.
Leave cells in PBST for 15 min during the third wash.
Incubate cells for 1 h with CAS-Block, optionally supplemented with 5% horse serum.
Dilute guinea pig anti-insulin (DAKO, A0564) at 1:300 and goat anti-somatostatin (Santa Cruz Biotechnology, SC-7819) at 1:200 in CAS-Block.
Incubate with primary antibodies for 1–3 h at room temperature or overnight at 4°C.
Wash cells three times with PBST.
Dilute secondary antibodies from Jackson ImmunoResearch at 1:200 in CAS-Block and incubate for 1 h at room temperature.
Wash cells three times with PBST.
Stain nuclei for 10 min using 1 μg/mL DAPI in ddH₂O.
Wash DAPI with PBS.
Mount slides before imaging if using plastic coverslips.
Aspirate culture medium following desired time of culture.
Wash the cells once with PBS.
Treat cells with 0.025% trypsin diluted 1:2 in PBS for 12 min in 37°C.
Dissociate the cells by pipetting up and down 10–15 times using a 1 ml pipette tip.
Transfer the cell suspension to Eppendorf tubes containing 100 μL FBS (for quenching of trypsin).
Centrifuge the cells for 5 min at 500 × g.
Wash the cells twice with FACS buffer (PBS, 2 mM EDTA, 2.5% FBS).
Centrifuge again for 5 min at 500 × g and aspirate FACS buffer.
Resuspend the cell pellet in fixable viability dye eFluor450 diluted 1:1,000 in FACS buffer to label dead cells.
Stain for dead cells to obtain reliable flow cytometry results.
Incubate for 30 minutes on ice.
Wash the cells once by centrifugation at 500 × g for 5 minutes.
Resuspend the cells in FACS buffer.
Pass the cell suspension through a 35 μm cell strainer to deplete clumps if cell sorting is required.
Gate living cells based on fixable viability dye eFluor450 stain.
Sort desired populations of cells directly into lysis buffer supplemented with RNA extraction kit.
Proceed with RNA extraction and follow standard protocols for qPCR or library preparation for RNA sequencing.
Fix the cells in 4% PFA in PBS for 10 minutes if analyzing hormone production with intracellular staining is required.
Centrifuge at 600 × g for 5 minutes after fixing.
Resuspend the cell pellet in PBST.
Follow the protocol for immune-staining with 600 × g, 5-minute centrifugations between stages.
Pass the cell suspension through a 35 μm cell strainer to deplete clumps if analyzing hormone production is required.
Take the cells to the flow cytometer.
Gate living cells based on fixable viability dye eFluor450 stain.
Aspirate the medium from day 5 cells.
Wash the cells once with RPMI medium and aspirate.
Add 300 μL of RPMI medium to each well.
Incubate plates for 3 days.
Collect all medium from each well on day 8 into Eppendorf tubes.
Centrifuge samples at maximum speed for 10 min.
Transfer supernatant to new Eppendorf tubes or 96-well plates.
Discard the pellets.
Add 1 mL of PBS supplemented with 2.5% FBS to each well.
Harvest cells using a cell scraper and transfer suspensions into Eppendorf tubes.
Add 2.5% FBS to PBS for improved pelleting of exocrine cells after centrifugation.
Centrifuge cells at 600 × g for 5 min.
Aspirate all supernatant and discard it.
Resuspend the cell pellet using 30 μL lysis buffer.
Measure insulin in the supernatant and cell lysates using Insulin ultra-sensitive kit according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Measure protein content in the cell lysates using Bio-Rad protein assay.
Calculate total secreted insulin, insulin content in cell lysates, and protein content in lysates.
Normalize secreted and content of insulin to total protein.
